name: pycryptodome
entry_points_source: Doc/src/signature/signature.rst, lines 25-37: a signature is verified with the verify method of a verifier object, which takes the hash and the incoming signature and raises ValueError if the message is not authentic; lib/Crypto/Signature defines verify for pkcs1_15, pss, eddsa, mldsa and DSS (DSS.py, line 127: ':raise ValueError: if the signature is not authentic'). Doc/src/guides/hashing.rst, lines 92-103: a MAC tag is checked with verify() or hexverify(), which HMAC, CMAC, Poly1305, KMAC128, BLAKE2b and BLAKE2s define (lib/Crypto/Hash). Doc/src/cipher/aes.rst, lines 36-43 and 175-182: the authenticated modes check the received tag with verify or decrypt_and_verify (their modules in lib/Crypto/Cipher also define hexverify), and the KW and KWP modes unwrap a key with unseal. Doc/src/guides/public_key_encryption.rst, lines 50-60: HPKE unseal() raises ValueError if the data was modified. Doc/src/io/kdf_limits.rst, lines 145-152, and Doc/src/protocol/kdf.rst, lines 101-124: bcrypt_check verifies a password against a bcrypt hash (lib/Crypto/Protocol/KDF.py, line 810: 'ValueError: if the password does not match'). Entry points are names, so the same names elsewhere in the package count too. Not entry points: new, the constructor of every cipher, hash and signature scheme, and decrypt, the decryption method of every cipher, which verify nothing in most of them (the decrypt of lib/Crypto/Cipher/oaep.py and the new of lib/Crypto/Protocol/HPKE.py, which reject invalid input, are left out with them); and the functions that import keys or remove padding, which parse.
rejection_bases_source: Doc/src/exceptions.rst, lines 6-15: errors are reported with the standard Python exceptions, ValueError when a value is not acceptable, for instance a message whose MAC tag does not match in decrypt_and_verify or in the verify method of a signature scheme, and the dedicated exceptions are all subclasses of ValueError. The docstrings of the entry points name ValueError: lib/Crypto/Signature/DSS.py, line 127; lib/Crypto/Hash/HMAC.py, line 196; lib/Crypto/Cipher/_mode_gcm.py, lines 679-680; lib/Crypto/Cipher/_mode_kw.py, lines 109-110; lib/Crypto/Protocol/HPKE.py, line 369; lib/Crypto/Protocol/KDF.py, lines 808-810.
